generated.title: M6.3 Earthquake Strikes Near Vanuatu a Day After M6.0
generated.description:
A magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck 197 km northwest of Port-Olry, Vanuatu, on October 20, 2026 at 04:20 UTC, at a depth of 16 km, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). The event data has been reviewed by USGS.

It follows a magnitude 6.0 earthquake in the same area on October 19 (USGS event us6000u3bc, https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us6000u3bc), part of a continuing sequence of earthquakes northwest of Port-Olry. USGS also recorded several earthquakes of magnitude 5 and above in the area over the same period.

USGS issued a green PAGER alert for this earthquake. PAGER is a modeled estimate of potential fatalities and economic losses, not a report of what actually happened, and it does not by itself show whether there was any impact.

About the tsunami line in the video: the USGS record carries a tsunami flag for this event. That flag is a general indicator and is not a confirmation that a tsunami occurred or that any warning was issued. In the information we reviewed, no tsunami impacts, casualties or damage have been confirmed. This may change as more information becomes available.

Magnitude is the USGS value (Mww). Other agencies may publish different preliminary magnitudes for the same earthquake.

Official event page: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us6000u3jl
